items.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I mean that CD we did together, you had some of the greatest people on there — Bill Watrous, Jerome Richardson, Keter Betts, yourself.

ctx.x: So there was some use in that thing there.

Some use there, just conduct yourself in a nice manner. But I’ve gotten to play with some of the greatest man. I mean that CD we did together, you had some of the greatest people on there — Bill Watrous, Jerome Richardson, Keter Betts, yourself.

items.title: Bill Watrous interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 26, 1999
items.q: It’s the same with Wendell. Both of us played on one of those tunes that you had the other day

ctx.x: Is it possible for you to describe to a younger player or even me, what do you think about when you improvise? Is it the chords that are behind you? Are you thinking about what you played six measures ago and where you’re going with it? Is it possible to put that into words?

I’m thinking ahead frankly. And what I’m basically doing is I’m thinking counterpoint as I’m going. And I’m listening to the textures that the rhythm section is putting out. I’m listening very carefully to the bass and drums and the piano and trying to get a mattress to bounce on so to speak. And if everything is planned, understandable, that’s coming down, then it’s not difficult, no problem at all to just close my eyes and go and play. It’s the same with Wendell. Both of us played on one of those tunes that you…
I was blown away by that.
